title: Shape Create & Edit Project
question: Choose the composition that should govern both Create Project and Edit Project. All options preserve the same fields, validation, permissions, and business behavior.

options.label: Readiness Console
options.lineage: operational launch checklist and control console
options.thesis: One focused setup workspace paired with a live readiness rail that explains what is required, optional, complete, or blocked.
options.viewport: Create opens on Essentials in a broad central work area while a compact right rail shows readiness, optional enrichments, and the Create Project action; Edit reuses the shell with a status overview and persistent save state.
options.risk: The readiness rail must remain concise or it becomes a competing form summary.

options.label: Project Dossier
options.lineage: structured client dossier with indexed sections
options.thesis: Treat each project as a concise operational dossier: identity first, evidence sources second, ongoing systems last.
options.viewport: A slim sticky chapter index sits beside a continuous document-like workspace; Create progressively reveals enrichment chapters, while Edit supports direct section jumps and an always-visible change ledger.
options.risk: A long dossier needs excellent section wayfinding to avoid feeling like a conventional settings page.

options.label: Command Deck
options.thesis: Lead with the operator’s task—launch, track, connect, automate, or tune AI—then reveal the exact controls needed for that task.
options.viewport: A top task deck summarizes five operational areas; the selected workbench fills the page below, with Create emphasizing launch requirements and Edit emphasizing current state, bulk tracking, and quick access.
options.risk: Task cards can resemble a generic dashboard unless the selected workbench remains visually dominant.
